record.paper_title: Boundary and Defect CFT: Open Problems and Applications
record.original_question: Do there exist monotonicity theorems for boundaries or defects in dimensions higher than two that generalize the two-dimensional g-theorem for boundary conformal field theories?

evidence.quote: Are there boundary or defect ‘c-theorems’ generalizing the g-theorem [208,209] of two-dimensional bCFT to higher dimensions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let a boundary conformal field theory (bCFT) in two spacetime dimensions be specified by a bulk conformal field theory together with a conformally invariant boundary condition. Affleck and Ludwig's g-theorem asserts that the boundary entropy g, defined from the overlap of the boundary state with the conformally invariant vacuum, decreases monotonically along any boundary renormalization group flow that connects two boundary fixed points (with the bulk theory held fixed).

Question: In dimensions d > 2, do there exist analogous "boundary c-theorems" or "defect c-theorems"? That is, can one define a real-valued quantity B[\mathcal{D}], attached either to a conformal boundary condition or to a p-dimensional conformal defect \mathcal{D} (1 ≤ p < d) embedded in a d-dimensional conformal field theory, such that:

(i) B[\mathcal{D}] depends only on the defect/boundary conformal data (and not on the choice of regularization scheme),
(ii) B[\mathcal{D}_{UV}] ≥ B[\mathcal{D}_{IR}] along every renormalization group flow on the defect (or boundary) that interpolates between two conformal endpoints \mathcal{D}_{UV} and \mathcal{D}_{IR}, with the bulk theory unchanged,
(iii) B reduces to (a function of) the Affleck–Ludwig boundary entropy g when d = 2 and the defect is a boundary?

Identify such candidate quantities B for each codimension and dimension, and prove the corresponding monotonicity theorem.
artifact.category_tag: boundary/defect conformal field theory and RG monotonicity
artifact.status_search_result: Substantial progress has been made since the question was posed. For pointlike (codimension-d) defects in general spacetime dimension, Casini, Salazar Landea, and Torroba (2022–2023) proved an entropic g-theorem using monotonicity of relative entropy. For 2d surface defects (b-theorem) and for boundaries in d=3 (boundary F-theorem-type results), monotonicity theorems have also been established by Jensen–O'Bannon, Kobayashi–Nishioka–Sato–Watanabe, Casini and collaborators, and others. However, a fully general defect c-theorem covering all codimensions and dimensions remains open, so the broad question is partially solved.

status_evidence.title: The entropic g-theorem in general spacetime dimension
status_evidence.snippet: Establishes the irreversibility of RG flows on a pointlike defect inserted in a d-dimensional Lorentzian CFT via quantum relative entropy.
status_evidence.claim: Pointlike-defect g-theorem proved in general spacetime dimensions.

status_evidence.title: Towards a C-theorem in defect CFT
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes that the increment of the regularized sphere free energy due to a defect does not increase under defect RG flows.
status_evidence.claim: Defect F-/C-theorem candidates formulated and tested.

status_evidence.title: Constraint on Defect and Boundary Renormalization Group Flows (Jensen–O'Bannon)
status_evidence.snippet: Derives monotonicity constraints on boundary and defect RG flows.
status_evidence.claim: Boundary/defect RG monotonicity results in dimensions higher than two.

status_evidence.title: Defect localized entropy: Renormalization group and holography
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses monotonic defect entropies along RG flows.
status_evidence.claim: Further developments toward higher-dimensional defect c-theorems.
